text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein and PLO leader Yasser Arafat emphasise the need to resist negative repercussions of the Israeli decisions in Palestinian areas, agree that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's moves are in breach of international legitimacy.
- Freezer trucks carrying Jordanian produce enter Lebanon after resolving a dispute over Jordan's agricultural exports.
- Arafat says Jordanian support is a "healer to Palestinian wounds".
- Jordanian-Palestinian leadership stress need to intensify contacts with major world capitals to put pressure on Israel.
- Lawyers union elections result in pan-Arabists gaining lion's share with Islamists trailing behind.
- Troubled Amman Investment Bank owns 20 percent of Jordan Spinning and Weaving.
- Finance Minister says that Jordan was moving ahead in its privatisation plan and expects EU accord during the coming months.
- Customs enforce measures to combat corruption.
- King, Arafat voice determination to face all challenges, joint committee meeting in Gaza arrives at agreement to step up cooperation in all areas.
- Government officals see fresh mandate for Kabariti in king's comments on television, but others have different interpretation of what king said.
